key_insight: Encoder–decoder operator learning becomes resolution-independent by analyzing the induced kernels in the limit, so both theory and error bounds can be stated without tying regularity to a specific discretization.
engineering_relevance: This gives practitioners a way to design and compare operator-learning models across different mesh, sensor, or basis resolutions while still predicting how optimization, encoding, and finite-width effects scale.
method: Map matrix-valued kernels on encoded data to operator-valued kernels on function spaces via RKHS isometries.
Prove convergence of induced kernels to a limiting kernel using operator-norm convergence of the associated integral operators.
Derive upper and lower error bounds for regularized SGD and extend the framework to encoder–decoder NTKs and neural networks.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical upper and lower bounds for decreasing and fixed step sizes, plus polynomial complexity guarantees when encoding errors decay algebraically.
watch_item: The guarantees rely on encoding errors decaying at a controlled rate and include additional finite-width terms, so real implementations may be sensitive to representation choice and network width.
paper_title: Resolution-Independent Analysis of Encoder--Decoder Operator Learning via Limiting Kernels
